ratings_why.fun: Leave-it-alone versus feed-it gives a real choice every turn, and Awaken thresholds give a payoff you can see coming; the routing cards are harder to read than they are fun.
ratings_why.distinct: Age as pips that can be moved, sold on and spent is new, but the Long Sleep build reads close to Hedgerow folk's turns-in-slot clocks.

verdict_why: Mother Ribica, Brother Netopir and Lamplighter Hrošč can't be read as written; the tribe's idea is sound and needs only those words fixed.

points.text: Mother Ribica's "each time they gain that much more Age" is unclear: it doesn't say whether spent or moved Age counts. Say "Awakens again each time it reaches N more Age than when it last Awakened."
Brother Netopir's "onto it" could mean Netopir or the new unit. Say "onto the unit you played", and say what happens when Netopir sits at the end of a row.
Lamplighter Hrošč doesn't say whether checks like the Seven-Month Dormouse's "2 or more Age" count double. List what it does double: stats and damage worked out from Age.
Give the board a sleeping-eye mark on Still units nobody has touched this turn, plus a crown on the oldest and a cradle on the youngest, so the Painter, Novice and Echo Bat read at a glance.
Kurent Bellman's cowbells should wake sleepers, not lull them: maybe "units next to this count 1 extra Age towards Awaken", so the carnival demon reads in what he does.

standouts.why: A blind olm hitting the weakest enemy by sensing pressure: clear text, and the lore is right there in what it does.
Parkelj, the scandalous black olm who moves, is the one card that breaks Still, so the story and the rule are the same thing.
Echo Bat carrying a sold unit's Age to the newest unit is the bats carrying the word, in one readable line.

weakest.why: Mother Ribica's repeat rule is the hardest text in the tribe to read, on a key card.
Lamplighter Hrošč is a rules note with a parenthetical; the beetle tending useless lamps doesn't come through.
Kurent Bellman is a flat aura with no carnival in it.

flags.note: Golden Brother Netopir copies Age from nothing; with golden Echo Bat or Mother Ribica it could feed the Eldest's Awaken 20 very fast.
Beehive Painter's X is the oldest unit's Age, and Hrošč doubles it, so big Age stacks give big buffs every turn.
The Eldest's Awaken 20 doubles the whole board, a big one-off spike worth the owner's eye.
"Each time they gain that much more Age" doesn't say how spent or moved Age counts.
"Onto it" is ambiguous, and the end-of-row case isn't covered.
It isn't clear which Age checks count double.
